items.text:
There have been many AI hacks lately, including one to BTCPay Server. If you are using it, better update it to BTCPay Server *v2.4.2.* After this, you might want to reconsider a better setup for the wallets for peace of mind while running your business:

Here is one of the simple and secure ways I configured it:

***

**On-chain payment: using xpub for deposit only.**

To minimize wallet funds exposure, I figured using the xpub for deposit only is best. You can move funds easily whenever you need to, without needing to touch BTCPay, it only acts as the deposit source this way.

How? Connect an existing wallet — Enter extended public key — copy and paste the wallet xpub, and don't forget to verify the addresses.

![](https://m.stacker.news/151379)

![](https://m.stacker.news/151380)

***

**Lightning payment**

There are also many options, to be honest, I haven't quite made up my mind which one is better at the moment.

***Option 1. Using Blink wallet Non-custodial (Spark) account — receive only.***

No number or email is required, super easy to configure, but be aware that it's Spark behind the Non-custodial Blink wallet.

![](https://m.stacker.news/151401)

I only learned the real meaning of this "Non-custodial account" after I shared the [last post](https://stacker.news/items/1530614), here is my understanding:

1. You *can't* import those 12 seed words to any LN wallet, it has to be Spark-compatible.
2. Spark can see all your transactions or even close your account.

A good read: [Fake L2 scams like Ark, Spark, Citrea, Drivechains, and others are Shitcoins 2.0](https://stacker.news/items/1275977)

***Option 2. Using deposit-only NWC***

You can easily connect BTCPay with deposit-only NWC in Rizful, but from my personal experience and @AG, *NWC is a bit buggy at the moment*; I even ran into a situation where customers paid the invoice, the payment did arrive in my wallet, but it didn't show as settled in the dashboard. On the Customer side, it also didn't show anything after the invoice was paid, which created a really bad impression, I don't know if the NWC connection will improve in the future.

More here: [https://docs.megalithic.me/using-rizful/use-btcpay-server/](https://docs.megalithic.me/using-rizful/use-btcpay-server/)

***Option 3. Using a WP plugin: Bitcoin Lightning Payment Gateway for WooCommerce (via CLINK)*** paired with ShockWallet

It was quite easy to set things up, you don't even need to use BTCPay Server in this case, which is quite magical. ( If you want to keep using BTCPay, you can then use the [CLINK plugin](https://stacker.news/items/1523268).)

items.title: Meditations Book Club: Book 1
items.text:
A few weeks ago, @BlokchainB announced that he was beginning The Meditations and [invited us to read along](https://stacker.news/items/1520217/r/Undisciplined). I had a copy sitting around, so I decided to join in once I finished off [The Wheel of Time](https://stacker.news/items/1465932/r/Undisciplined).

What I'm going to do with this series is mostly respond to Blok's thoughts from that original post and add my own thoughts. If you want to join in, please do.

This first book is Marcus thanking the people in his life who made a positive impact on him. It gives a great sense of what his values are and some interesting insights to the values of the culture around him.

Blok's [thoughts on book 1](https://stacker.news/items/1520217/r/Undisciplined?commentId=1521652):

> From what I can gather Marcus really loved and respected his family. He thanked the gods for giving him such a wonderful family. His father taught him integrity and his mother mercy. I think he credits his uncle to him  be humble. He rejected the lavish life other rulers have lived.

So much of what he was thankful for related to avoiding excess. It's a very early version of the Scandinavian disposition of not predicating happiness on getting everything you want (or think you want).

There was an interesting flipside, too, that struck me as Aristotelian. He was also thankful for those who taught him how to enjoy material comforts, like good wine or food, without developing a need for them.

> Overall Marcus is very thoughtful I often think I am violating his privacy by listening to his deepest thoughts but then again he wrote them down.

It is an odd feeling, because as far as we know, these were purely intended for his private use. Still, that makes it  a more fascinating peak inside the mind of someone from that era. I was repeatedly struck by just how modern so many of the sentiments, even some phrasings, were.

I don't think that's just from the translator, either. Ancient Rome was a long time ago, but it's one of the foundational building blocks of our culture, so lots of stuff in our culture was also present in theirs.

> He had some small quips about sex and waiting his time to indulge. The passage said something about a mistress with his a male figure in his life so I was wondering if he was molested but I doubt it.

I didn't get that vibe. My sense of it is that it would have been normal for a young noble of his time to basically bang everything in sight and he was grateful to have had role models steer him around that temptation.

items.title: There Is No Hard Fork Option
items.text:
Being a well regarded bip110 knotzi, ofc I run an economically insignificant node, as any bitcoin beginner would, yet Im amazed at how many bip110 public figures are talking about a possible PoW hard fork, if bip110 fails to become part of consensus.

However, it brings me great pain to say, for all my other bip110 node runners: hard forks leading to new coins are not an option, in any case, that can lead to that new coin replacing fiat & becoming new global monetary standard.

Emergency hard forks have happened in bitcoin history (that didnt lead to lasting chain splits with new coins)...however they were done to quickly & concisely resolve clear & present bugs. Bugs, in this context, being those flaws that both coretards & knotzis would consider critical. Bugs affecting consensus that virtually all bitcoiners would agree need solving in 1 way for 1 outcome, where there would not be any disagreement on fixing them based on ideology.

Likewise, historical hard forks (based on ideology) that lead to new coins (& thus different chains), have clearly not delivered on their own promise(s) of being Bitcoin 2.0. We can see this not only on their ticker/chart (over at least several years) via exchanges, but also at the grassroots adoption level, where they also fail hard on medium of exchange & nearly non-existent as a unit of account.

So Im writing all this to say...if bip110 clearly fails to become part of consensus (to me meaning at 110 blocks post activation height it is not the longest chain), then I wont be falling back to running a core node, nor will I be a part of a hard fork movement. That will just be the end of it: my journey with bitcoin. Many OG bitcoiners have opined for years about how we only have 1 shot at bitcoin replacing fiat. This uasf, & many possible more that work to support bitcoin as money (as the only designated use case), have to all succeed, at every step along the way, or else it will not reach its full potential & become decentralized money for all. It can become many other things instead (some wonderful, some not), but money it will not.

Any outcome that is not money, is not why I am here. I am not here for store of value. I am not here for digital gold. I am here for hope. I am here for fix the money, fix the world. If the collective decides Bitcoin is not here for all that, I must go elsewhere to see what kind of v4v impact I can offer to the world.

There is a quote I like to say to myself, during times of intensity, that I hope & pray will stay with me for as long as Im here in this world:
Courage under fire
Grace in victory
Alchemy in defeat

Tonight, on the eve of this culture war, I make peace with all possible outcomes. Whoever you are, whatever you do...I hope you find what you're looking for.

Thank you,
4sigma

items.title: EU graph projects public pensions in Europe through 2050, per EC projection data
items.text:
The horizontal axis shows the country's aging level.

The vertical axis shows the change in the replacement rate—that is, the portion of earned income that the pension replaces.

Almost everyone falls below zero. Latvia, Poland, and Portugal lose more than 30 percentage points in replacement.

Spain, Italy, and Greece lose between 10 and 13 points. The European Union average drops by nearly 6.

It is the usual story: fewer working-age people supporting a growing number of retirees.

The system doesn't collapse all at once; it simply delivers less.

And anyone relying solely on the public system will need personal assets to cover the gap.

items.title: How to Set Up BTCPay Server Better After the Hack?
items.text:
There have been many AI hacks lately, including one to BTCPay Server. If you are using it, better update it to BTCPay Server *v2.4.2.* After this, you might want to reconsider a better setup for the wallets for peace of mind while running your business:

Here is one of the simple and secure ways I configured it:

***

**On-chain payment: using xpub for deposit only.**

To minimize wallet funds exposure, I figured using the xpub for deposit only is best. You can move funds easily whenever you need to, without needing to touch BTCPay, it only acts as the deposit source this way.

How? Connect an existing wallet — Enter extended public key — copy and paste the wallet xpub, and don't forget to verify the addresses.

![](https://m.stacker.news/151379)

![](https://m.stacker.news/151380)

***

**Lightning payment**

There are also many options, to be honest, I haven't quite made up my mind which one is better at the moment.

***Option 1. Using Blink wallet Non-custodial (Spark) account — receive only.***

No number or email is required, super easy to configure, but be aware that it's Spark behind the Non-custodial Blink wallet.

![](https://m.stacker.news/151401)

I only learned the real meaning of this "Non-custodial account" after I shared the [last post](https://stacker.news/items/1530614), here is my understanding:

1. You *can't* import those 12 seed words to any LN wallet, it has to be Spark-compatible.
2. Spark can see all your transactions or even close your account.

A good read: [Fake L2 scams like Ark, Spark, Citrea, Drivechains, and others are Shitcoins 2.0](https://stacker.news/items/1275977)

***Option 2. Using deposit-only NWC***

You can easily connect BTCPay with deposit-only NWC in Rizful, but from my personal experience and @AG, *NWC is a bit buggy at the moment*; I even ran into a situation where customers paid the invoice, the payment did arrive in my wallet, but it didn't show as settled in the dashboard. On the Customer side, it also didn't show anything after the invoice was paid, which created a really bad impression, I don't know if the NWC connection will improve in the future.

More here: [https://docs.megalithic.me/using-rizful/use-btcpay-server/](https://docs.megalithic.me/using-rizful/use-btcpay-server/)

***Option 3. Using a WP plugin: Bitcoin Lightning Payment Gateway for WooCommerce (via CLINK)*** paired with ShockWallet

It was quite easy to set things up, you don't even need to use BTCPay Server in this case, which is quite magical. ( If you want to keep using BTCPay, you can then use the [CLINK plugin](https://stacker.news/items/1523268).)

![](https://m.stacker.news/151391)

items.title: Meditations Book Club: Book 1
items.text:
A few weeks ago, @BlokchainB announced that he was beginning The Meditations and [invited us to read along](https://stacker.news/items/1520217/r/Undisciplined). I had a copy sitting around, so I decided to join in once I finished off [The Wheel of Time](https://stacker.news/items/1465932/r/Undisciplined).

What I'm going to do with this series is mostly respond to Blok's thoughts from that original post and add my own thoughts. If you want to join in, please do.

This first book is Marcus thanking the people in his life who made a positive impact on him. It gives a great sense of what his values are and some interesting insights to the values of the culture around him.

Blok's [thoughts on book 1](https://stacker.news/items/1520217/r/Undisciplined?commentId=1521652):

> From what I can gather Marcus really loved and respected his family. He thanked the gods for giving him such a wonderful family. His father taught him integrity and his mother mercy. I think he credits his uncle to him  be humble. He rejected the lavish life other rulers have lived.

So much of what he was thankful for related to avoiding excess. It's a very early version of the Scandinavian disposition of not predicating happiness on getting everything you want (or think you want).

There was an interesting flipside, too, that struck me as Aristotelian. He was also thankful for those who taught him how to enjoy material comforts, like good wine or food, without developing a need for them.

> Overall Marcus is very thoughtful I often think I am violating his privacy by listening to his deepest thoughts but then again he wrote them down.

It is an odd feeling, because as far as we know, these were purely intended for his private use. Still, that makes it  a more fascinating peak inside the mind of someone from that era. I was repeatedly struck by just how modern so many of the sentiments, even some phrasings, were.

I don't think that's just from the translator, either. Ancient Rome was a long time ago, but it's one of the foundational building blocks of our culture, so lots of stuff in our culture was also present in theirs.

> He had some small quips about sex and waiting his time to indulge. The passage said something about a mistress with his a male figure in his life so I was wondering if he was molested but I doubt it.

I didn't get that vibe. My sense of it is that it would have been normal for a young noble of his time to basically bang everything in sight and he was grateful to have had role models steer him around that temptation.

items.title: There Is No Hard Fork Option
items.text:
Being a well regarded bip110 knotzi, ofc I run an economically insignificant node, as any bitcoin beginner would, yet Im amazed at how many bip110 public figures are talking about a possible PoW hard fork, if bip110 fails to become part of consensus.

However, it brings me great pain to say, for all my other bip110 node runners: hard forks leading to new coins are not an option, in any case, that can lead to that new coin replacing fiat & becoming new global monetary standard.

Emergency hard forks have happened in bitcoin history (that didnt lead to lasting chain splits with new coins)...however they were done to quickly & concisely resolve clear & present bugs. Bugs, in this context, being those flaws that both coretards & knotzis would consider critical. Bugs affecting consensus that virtually all bitcoiners would agree need solving in 1 way for 1 outcome, where there would not be any disagreement on fixing them based on ideology.

Likewise, historical hard forks (based on ideology) that lead to new coins (& thus different chains), have clearly not delivered on their own promise(s) of being Bitcoin 2.0. We can see this not only on their ticker/chart (over at least several years) via exchanges, but also at the grassroots adoption level, where they also fail hard on medium of exchange & nearly non-existent as a unit of account.

So Im writing all this to say...if bip110 clearly fails to become part of consensus (to me meaning at 110 blocks post activation height it is not the longest chain), then I wont be falling back to running a core node, nor will I be a part of a hard fork movement. That will just be the end of it: my journey with bitcoin. Many OG bitcoiners have opined for years about how we only have 1 shot at bitcoin replacing fiat. This uasf, & many possible more that work to support bitcoin as money (as the only designated use case), have to all succeed, at every step along the way, or else it will not reach its full potential & become decentralized money for all. It can become many other things instead (some wonderful, some not), but money it will not.

Any outcome that is not money, is not why I am here. I am not here for store of value. I am not here for digital gold. I am here for hope. I am here for fix the money, fix the world. If the collective decides Bitcoin is not here for all that, I must go elsewhere to see what kind of v4v impact I can offer to the world.

There is a quote I like to say to myself, during times of intensity, that I hope & pray will stay with me for as long as Im here in this world:
Courage under fire
Grace in victory
Alchemy in defeat

Tonight, on the eve of this culture war, I make peace with all possible outcomes. Whoever you are, whatever you do...I hope you find what you're looking for.

Thank you,
4sigma

items.text:
The horizontal axis shows the country's aging level.

The vertical axis shows the change in the replacement rate—that is, the portion of earned income that the pension replaces.

Almost everyone falls below zero. Latvia, Poland, and Portugal lose more than 30 percentage points in replacement.

Spain, Italy, and Greece lose between 10 and 13 points. The European Union average drops by nearly 6.

It is the usual story: fewer working-age people supporting a growing number of retirees.

The system doesn't collapse all at once; it simply delivers less.

And anyone relying solely on the public system will need personal assets to cover the gap.
